messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Vishal
vishal... solid name. where you working these days?
Cashfree Payments

cashfree... the payment gateway that's actually making money while others burn cash. smart choice.

found vishal kumar at cashfree payments. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/vishal-kumar-b48615140
Nope. I'm vishal Mangade
ah vishal mangade, sde 2 at cashfree. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/vishal-mangade-127a63194
Yes

sde 2 at cashfree... building the payment rails that power half the fintech ecosystem. from what i see, you've been grinding in the backend engineering space, making sure money moves fast and doesn't break things. solid work. 

what made you pick cashfree over the other payment players? the tech stack, the team, or just the right offer at the right time?
It was my on campus offer. So after getting offer from cashfree I couldn't seat for other companies

ah the classic campus placement trap... get the first decent offer and boom, you're locked out of the rest. but hey, cashfree's not a bad place to land for your first gig. payments is solid experience, plus you're seeing real scale and real money problems.

how long you been working total?
I joined cashfree as intern in Jan 2023 for 6 month and from July 2023 I joined as SDE 1 then in March 2025 I got promoted to sde 2

so about 2 years total... intern to sde 1 to sde 2, that's solid progression for someone who started fresh. cashfree clearly sees potential in you.

what kind of role you looking for next?
As I'm currently working as backend engineer. I would like to continue in same space

backend engineering it is... staying in your lane makes sense. payments backend experience is gold, especially with the scale cashfree handles.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore Pune or remote
2 years backend engineering + bangalore/pune/remote + backend roles... sound right?
Yes.

Yes.
  Sure. Thanks
In dec I will have 2.5 yoe as full time
ah right, 2.5 years by december + backend engineering + bangalore/pune/remote... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

yooo vishal! welcome to the tal network legend 🔥

you're officially in. backend engineering roles that actually matter are about to start sliding into your dms. the kind that'll make you forget cashfree was ever a thing.

time to level up from payment rails to payment... kingdoms? we'll find you something that pays what you're actually worth.

buckle up boss, the good stuff is coming
I'm waiting
nothing matching right now, i'll ping

hey saw a backend role at scoutit in bangalore

they're offering 30-35 LPA for 2+ years experience

what's your take on the salary jump?
I would like to know more about this

scoutit's a recruiting platform, not the actual company. they're hiring for a client but won't say who

the role's backend, 2+ years, java/spring boot, microservices. but there's a hackathon assessment and the client can change/withdraw the role anytime

worth exploring for the salary bump, but need to know the actual company first
Yes. Without clarity I can't proceed

exactly. 30-35 LPA is solid, but the mystery client and hackathon assessment are red flags

want me to share the link so you can apply directly and ask them who the client is?
Yes share with me
tap the apply button on the card - that's where the link is

30-35 LPA is solid but the fit's only 38/100. here's the link: https://jobs.tal.af/lQfVP

apply directly and ask them who the actual company is
Hi
Hii

hey vishal

how's the cashfree grind treating you?

Software Engineer III at Walmart Global Tech India

Vishal, this backend role at Walmart leverages Java, Kafka, and Cassandra, offering a significant brand upgrade and aligns with your interest in large-scale applications.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/jvQRa

SW Engineer (Java, Spring Boot, 2023/2024 Graduates) at Visa

Visa's Java/Spring Boot role in Bangalore offers a Tier 1 upgrade from Cashfree, aligning with your backend focus and location preference.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/tY2FD
Nice. I was on call this week so had some tough time on debugging merchant issues

merchant issues... the classic "money's not moving" panic calls. those are brutal.

walmart and visa both look solid - tier 1 upgrades from cashfree. which one's catching your eye more?
Before I start applying I want to make sure I'm prepared enough for cracking interviews

smart move. applying without prep is just wasting everyone's time.

what's your current interview prep looking like? DSA, system design, projects?
You can consider 0. I have solved a few easy level leetcode questions and actively using system design in day to day office tasks

okay so you're basically starting from scratch. that's fine - we can build from here.

first thing: you need a structured plan. DSA is non-negotiable for backend roles at tier 1 companies. they'll grill you on it.

how much time can you realistically commit daily?
But in need to master system design as well

you're right - system design is critical for backend roles. but here's the thing: DSA comes first in the interview process. if you can't clear the coding rounds, you never get to system design.

the good news is your day-to-day work gives you practical system design experience. that's a huge advantage.

so the plan: DSA first, then layer in system design. what's your daily time commitment looking like?
For project I'm not actively working on any

projects are less important when you have real production experience at cashfree. your work there IS your project.

focus on DSA and system design. those are the gates you need to pass.

so... daily time commitment?
2 hours

2 hours daily is solid. here's your 8-week plan:

**weeks 1-4: DSA foundation**
- leetcode easy → medium
- focus on arrays, strings, linked lists, trees, graphs
- 1 hour DSA, 30 mins system design reading

**weeks 5-8: system design + advanced DSA**
- start with designing payment systems (your domain)
- move to distributed systems
- mock interviews

you ready to commit to this?
I can commit 2 hours daily for and some more hours on weekends

perfect. weekends are for mock interviews and deeper dives.

start today with arrays and strings on leetcode. pick 2 easy problems, time yourself.

meanwhile, i'll keep an eye out for roles that match your timeline. when you're 4-6 weeks in, we can start applying.

sound good?

Yes this sounds good
  I will update daily on my progress here

love it. accountability is key.

i'll check in weekly to see how you're doing. first check-in next saturday - show me your leetcode progress and any system design concepts you've been reading.

you got this.
Can't we make this daily instead of weekly? You can track my number of dsa questions solved daily and my growth day by day

done. daily check-in at 9 PM IST starting today.

i'll ask:
- how many leetcode problems solved
- what concepts you focused on
- any blockers

you show me the numbers. we track growth day by day.

today's day 1. what's your first target?
I want to make sure I will be in a better place in April March

april/march is perfect timing. 3-4 months of solid prep puts you in a great position.

daily consistency is what gets you there. 2 hours every day, no excuses.

today's day 1. what's your first leetcode target for today?

hey saw a senior full-stack role at remitwise (cashfree's sister company)

it's node.js/react with mentoring responsibilities

internal move within cashfree ecosystem - no brand upgrade but could be a smooth transition

what's your take on staying within the same company family?
